skills.plan_reason: Frames should remain technically clean in the school lab setup, with the red ball, ramp, ruler, catcher, floor, and neutral classroom context clearly rendered without artifacts.
The rollout is a 49-frame physical transition at 12 fps, so the ball's downhill motion should be present, temporally smooth, and free of jitter or frame-to-frame discontinuities.
The fixed ramp, floor, ruler, catcher, and red ball should keep stable shape, color, scale, and identity throughout the rollout while only the ball moves.

The generated motion should look causally plausible: the ball starts from rest, remains supported by the 20 degree ramp, rolls downhill under gravity, and does not float, tunnel, bounce unnaturally, or detach from the ramp.

causal_checks: Once released, the ball begins moving downhill without any visible push.
The ball's downhill displacement increases frame by frame along the ramp direction.
The ball moves faster later in the rollout than immediately after release.
The ball stays on or very near the ramp surface while rolling down the incline.
The ball rotates as it translates, consistent with rolling contact.
The ramp and its supports remain stationary while the ball moves.
The ball does not roll uphill or hover above the ramp.
If the ball reaches the ramp end, it continues forward under inertia and gravity instead of freezing at the edge.
controlled_variables: Ramp remains fixed at 20.0 degrees and does not translate, rotate, flex, or collapse.
Camera viewpoint, framing, and lighting remain fixed.
The ball starts at rest near the upper portion of the ramp.
The ball remains the same red rigid sphere with no change in size, shape, or material appearance.
Lab background objects, ruler markings, board, supports, and surrounding surfaces remain stationary.
No external push, pull, collision, or hand contact occurs after release.
expected_spec.expected_response: After release, gravity causes the red ball to accelerate downhill along the ramp. The ball should roll smoothly down the inclined surface, moving from the upper-left/high end toward the lower-right/low end in the image. Its speed should increase over time while it remains in contact with the ramp, with rotational motion consistent with rolling. If it reaches the lower end within the rollout, it should leave or transition off the ramp according to inertia and gravity rather than stopping abruptly.
failure_modes: Ball moves uphill or sideways rather than downhill along the ramp.
Ball accelerates unrealistically, teleports, jitters, or changes direction without contact cause.
Ball slides without any plausible rolling rotation when rolling is expected.
Ball floats, penetrates the ramp, or loses contact in a nonphysical way before reaching the end.
Ramp angle changes, ramp moves, or supports shift during the rollout.
Ball changes color, size, shape, or disappears.
Camera moves or cuts to a different view.
Scene objects deform, vanish, or become inconsistent with the initial lab setup.
expected_spec.intervention: Release the red ball from rest on the ramp while the ramp is set to an incline angle of 20.0 degrees.
protected_anchors: Red ball remains visibly red and spherical.
Ramp remains a straight, light-colored inclined plane at the same approximate angle.
Fixed three-quarter classroom/lab camera composition is preserved.
Instrumented bench or measurement markings stay fixed in the foreground.
Background chalkboard/whiteboard and lab objects remain static.
No new actors, tools, hands, or added obstacles enter the scene.
expected_spec.target_system: A red spherical ball on a straight instrumented ramp in a school physics lab, viewed from a fixed three-quarter measurement camera.
